item.text: The directory only has the evaluation logs, so the implementation files are new. I’m going to add the five requested files with global-script structure and keep the behavior concentrated in the simulation state machine and elevator scheduler.

The shell, person factory, and world builder are in place. Next I’m adding the elevator as its own stateful scheduler, then the simulation loop and agent planner that drives the daily office behavior.

The elevator file now owns the five-state door/motion machine, capacity tracking, button lamps, and SCAN target selection. I’m adding `sim.js` with the clock, lighting keys, occupancy controls, reusable plan primitives, and worker/visitor lifecycle.

The full code is written, so I’m switching to verification: syntax checks, file read-back, and then I’ll fix any runtime-level issues that show up from static inspection before starting a local server.

Syntax checks passed. I found a couple of plan-construction issues in the static pass: some visitor branches walked to a randomized seat but then sat at a fixed waypoint, and upstairs visitors needed an explicit return ride because the plan is compiled before their `floor` field changes. I’m patching those now.
